prompt: Why does this code print the same value for both variables?
choices: b = a copies the reference — both a and b point to the same array in memory
int[] uses value semantics like primitives
explanation: Array assignment copies the reference, not the array. a and b point to the same int[]. Modifying b[0] modifies the shared array, so a[0] == 99. To get an independent copy: int[] b = Arrays.copyOf(a, a.length);
